summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter presented with worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and purulent urine. She was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis caused by E. coli, treated initially with IV ceftriaxone, and transitioned to oral cefpodoxime for completion of a two-week course. During admission, she was found to have a borderline diabetic HbA1c of 6.5%, prompting a scheduled follow-up with her primary care provider and dietary counseling. Her pain improved, she remained afebrile, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments, including reduced doses of amitriptyline and fluoxetine. Social work facilitated temporary housing through a family member due to her homelessness.
problems: Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
